introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between solids and liquids in terms of the following properties.

(i) Molecular arrangements

(ii) Intermolecular forces *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Molecular arrangement**

| | Solids | Liquids |
|---|---|---|
| Spacing | Molecules (atoms or ions) are packed very close together, in contact | Molecules are also close together, with a spacing only slightly larger than in the solid |
| Order | **Regular, ordered arrangement** (a crystal lattice with long-range order) | **Disordered arrangement**: only short-range order, no repeating pattern over large distances |
| Motion | Each molecule only **vibrates about a fixed position**; it cannot change neighbours | Molecules **move past one another** (slide, rotate and diffuse) and keep changing neighbours |

**(ii) Intermolecular forces**

| | Solids | Liquids |
|---|---|---|
| Strength | **Strong** forces of attraction between the molecules | **Weaker** forces than in a solid, but still considerable |
| Effect | The forces are strong enough to hold each molecule in a fixed position, so a solid has a **fixed shape and a fixed volume** | The forces keep the molecules together (so the liquid has a **fixed volume**) but cannot hold them in fixed positions, so the liquid **takes the shape of its container** and can flow |
| Energy | The molecules have the lowest potential energy and only vibrational kinetic energy | The molecules have more energy: on melting, the latent heat of fusion partly overcomes the forces and breaks down the regular lattice |
